storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Elegant, alluring—an Eastern "deity" of fatal charm.

Legend has it that when she lowers her fan, you will see the face of your most beloved reflected beneath.

Yet legends are merely legends. Pray that her gaze never falls upon you. Once she seeps into your memories like a pervasive night mist, nothing will remain of your mind but a delirious, hollow obsession.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
In A.F. @16@1, a cargo ship with no traceable voyage records or authorized paperwork silently docked at the Londinium Freight Harbor.

The vessel was later confirmed to have originated from a port in the ancient Panlong Empire of the Far East. On the night of its arrival, harbor workers and nearby residents reported a collective dream of an Eastern woman with raven hair, obsidian eyes, and skin like ivory.

Witnesses described her as both "fascinating" and "hauntingly familiar." Notably, several male witnesses exhibited catatonic symptoms while providing their accounts.

Mythag's Investigators searched the ship immediately. Strangely, despite pervasive sounds of giggling and high-level Gnostic Responses, no trace of a Silver Core was initially found.

The following day, Lord Dexter entered the hold. Inside a ceramic vase that had already been searched multiple times, he discovered a Silver Core enveloped in a thin, clinging mist. As of A.F. 314, this Silver Core was deemed "unawakenable" by all known methods.

It was not until the arrival of the current Keeper, @3, that the Silver Core awakened spontaneously. The resulting entity identifies herself as "Xu" and has requested a permanent link with @3.

—Excerpt from "Mythag University Silver Core Storage Records

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
Xu appeared on campus just as naturally as she once drifted through palaces, royal tents, and various societies in the Far East. No one can say for certain when she first appeared.

To all who meet her, she feels instinctively familiar—a long-lost friend, or perhaps a cherished lover—even if they have never shared a single moment of their lives.

Only a rare few among the Awakeners maintain a preternatural wariness of her. Or, more accurately, only those of exceptional power can detect the anomaly: Xu, clinging and pervasive like a mist, seeping into their memories.

 The Mythag Administration once debated whether she required strict containment, even considering the development of specialized countermeasures. Yet, Xu dissolved these anxieties with a series of clandestine deals and a single promise:

"My intentions do not lie with these little ones."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
...To offer sacrifice where none is due is named Profane Rites. It is a delusion that devours the wealth of the people, persisting despite every decree of prohibition.

The coastal folk are steeped in the habit of venerating false gods, driven by a passion for raising rustic shrines and unhallowed altars. Vast fortunes are squandered while fields and looms lie fallow, yet the hamlets remain blind to the rot within. Time and again, the magistrates raze these dens to the ground, only for them to sprout anew the moment the garrison withdraws.

Most grievous are the foreign vagabonds. Settling among our villages, they have taken their own sacred icons and turned them upside down, distorting them to resemble the sign for a "Well"—the character "井".

The deities enshrined therein—both the masters and their attendants—possess verifiable histories; they are largely women who met with violent or unjust ends. In the beginning, the flock consisted of mere peasant women, stage-players, and common streetwalkers.

But soon, wife brings husband, mother brings son, and the prostitute brings her patron. Having swollen in rank, they form shadow factions for private gain. It has become a dark wonder to see entire clusters of villages rally behind a single figure—some to infiltrate the halls of officialdom, others to raise private militias to wage war upon their neighbors.

@4@4@3@2
The following handwriting is illegible, except for several lines of very neat handwriting in @3. Translated by the Linguistics Department, the text reads:

<Italic:"Shameless old wretch. His views are so warped, his prose so utterly tedious. I was bored, so I raised a few crickets to watch them fight—and still, he must wag his tongue and prattle on about it..."

<Bold:"It's none of your damn business.">>

—Excerpt from a handwritten copy of <Italic:Wild Fox Study Gazetter>.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
Have you ever felt the world grow so deathly quiet that you felt the urge to shatter something, just to hear the sound?

Lust is the silver vase she hurls; the prey startled by its chime... they will slaughter for love and be slaughtered by love, until their spirit is bled dry and only a hollow shell remains.

Then, those drained husks will offer her ever greater dominion, staining everything in sight with a bloody, delicious chaos.

A chaos that never ends.

daily.title: Awaken
daily.content: I am Xu, the Mistress of the Dreamless Land. If, in your heart, there is one you ache to see, yet cannot attain, I shall lower my fan and grant you a glimpse.

daily.title: Upgrade: I
daily.content: Do you anticipate a greater beauty from me, or a greater dread?

daily.title: Upgrade: II
daily.content: Such attentiveness makes me want to tease you all the more.

daily.title: Upgrade: III
daily.content: These slight diversions are more to my liking than the offerings of my devotees.

daily.title: Enlighten: Observe
daily.content: There was once a Princess born of Pleasure. Her robes were threaded with gold, her skin like ivory, the scent of agarwood drifted around her, and the mere sweep of her gaze could steal a soul.

daily.title: Enlighten: Ponder
daily.content: I have almost forgotten her tale entirely, but it was one of Rapture, one of Cruelty, one that began with Abandonment and Retribution, and concluded with Sacrifice and Blind Obedience.

daily.title: Enlighten: Reflect
daily.content: She soon tired of the sport. Her devotees merely repeated the same theatre, consumed by the Love born of Lust, or the Lust born of Love. Their foolishness—their heartbreak over betrayal and loss—it bored her. Their tears, too, bored her.

daily.title: Enlighten: Insight
daily.content: First Their bearing, then Their shape, until They also possessed a pair of... or rather, until all that remained memorable was a pair of beautiful, Soul-Capturing Eyes—eyes just like mine.

daily.title: Enlighten: Elevate
daily.content:
Do you not love me? Then why cower when you are encompassed? Do you not loath me? Then why weep when there is no return?
Oh, now you fear my shadow? Has the fragrance of white magnolia become a cloying, inexplicable musk to you?

daily.title: Enlighten: Florish
daily.content:
Do not trouble yourself; you are not like those common multitude. 
Hush. Do not look behind me. Pay no mind to the unseen caress. Look into my eyes, and my eyes alone.

daily.title: Affinity: I
daily.content:
Ah, you stare, enraptured by my fan again? Hehe. No matter whose face you desire, I shall let you have it. Come, draw closer—
Oh? You refuse? Such cold words, yet such an adorable expression...

daily.title: Affinity: II
daily.content:
I am utterly bored this day. Is there no wish you require me to make manifest?

A pity you don't. So many are willing to wield the scythe and offer me sweetmeat for far more trifling ends.
But if it's you asking...

daily.title: Affinity: III
daily.content:
Why does the Order of the Swelling Grace follow me, and what was its genesis? An amusing query. Have you, too, known the person unattainable, or the regret of failed struggle?
Hmm, it seems not. What a waste. That look of desperate struggle—it would be so very amusing to behold on your face.

daily.title: Affinity: IV
daily.content:
You are truly a marvel, so preoccupied with the trivialities of the corporeal, in a world already marked for ruin.

It compels me to take an interest myself.

daily.title: Affinity: V
daily.content:
Beneath my fan, every soul sees the face of their most cherished. I lend this power to the weak, that they may wield it as a blade for my own amusement.

But perhaps—I only say, perhaps. If you were to be enthralled by it, I would know a true, unsullied Ecstasy.

daily.title: Chat: Touch
daily.content: ...If you continue to trespass thus, the guise I adopt for you may not remain so agreeable.

daily.title: Chat: About the Crisis
daily.content:
All things end in the Void. Why not seek some further pleasure with me before then?

Rest assured, should the day come that you cannot resist the Dissolution further, I shall not allow It to claim you first.

daily.title: Chat: About Mythag
daily.content: The University so firmly rejected my application for the psychological therapy office. How strange; what objection could they possibly hold?

daily.title: Chat: What I Like
daily.content: In the legends of the Panlong Empire, the peacock is a handsome, flamboyant, and malicious beast. Beautiful and viscious—it makes the heart race. Ugly and kind, however, is rather boring.

daily.title: Chat: What I Hate
daily.content:
All nascent beings are a bother. Small, soft, loud, they unconsciously command all things around them.

I enjoy a spectacle, but decidedly not that sort. Pray, ensure they remain far, far away.

daily.title: Chat: About the Keeper
daily.content:
You? You are my little Jasmine, my obedient darling, the delightful game of playhouse I so willingly participate in...
Ah, mere happy ravings. Please pay them no mind.

daily.title: Chat: About Sorel
daily.content:
That Madam in Red once sent me several invitations to her salons.
The foreign confections were passable, but... 
She ought to have informed me sooner that at her residence, "desserts" and "servants" were not synonymous.

daily.title: Chat: About Lily
daily.content: I, too, once had such a pretty, compliant girl. A tempting flower-bud, of course she needed a few thorns—she could not simply be placed in a vase.

daily.title: Chat: The Order of Swelling Grace
daily.content: Oh? You ask why they bore those marks under their arms? Do you not find it utterly diverting?

battle.title: Investigation Begins
battle.content: The gaze of such petty, common minds is an utter vexation to me.

battle.title: Investigation Success
battle.content: You ask why Their crania are so vacant? Hmm, perhaps it is merely Their nature.

battle.title: Investigation Halted
battle.content: ...This, at least, grants me a slight spark of interest.

battle.title: Skill: I
battle.content: Amuse me. Slay one another in pain and dread!

battle.title: Skill: II
battle.content: What is it you are looking for in my Dreamless Land?

battle.title: Rouse
battle.content: Hehe... Do any of you dare to behold my true form?

battle.title: Exalt
battle.content: Suffer no Fury, know no Resentment, for All is Nullity.

battle.title: Over-Exalt
battle.content: Think not, Trouble not; Listen Blindly, Obey Mutely, for the Mortal Coil is only Burden!
